config.title: Lantern Walks in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: Public St. Martin lantern walks in Berlin for November 2026, checked against the organisers' own pages on 22 October.

items.q: When is St. Martin's Day in Berlin this year?
items.a: **Wednesday 11 November 2026.** It is not a public holiday, so many walks are on that evening after work and school, and some move to the days around it: Thursday 12 in Halensee and Buckow, **Friday 13 in Lichtenberg** and **Saturday 14 at the Domäne Dahlem**.

items.q: Where are the biggest lantern walks in Berlin?
items.a: The **Lichtenberg walk** from Freiaplatz to the Hans-Zoschke-Stadion on Friday 13 November expects **1,000 to 1,500 people**. On 11 November, the **three walks to the Friedrich-Ludwig-Jahn-Sportpark** in Prenzlauer Berg and the **Berliner Dom** play with a walk round the Lustgarten draw big crowds too.

items.q: Do I need to book or pay for a lantern walk?
items.a: No. None of the ten public walks with a confirmed 2026 date asks for a ticket or a booking. Only the **lantern-making afternoons** at the Neu-Buckow church on 3 and 5 November ask you to register by email.

items.q: What time do lantern walks start?
items.a: Mostly **between 16:00 and 17:30**. The sun sets at **16:19** on 11 November and it is dark by about 16:56, so a walk that starts with a short service or play sets off just as the lanterns begin to glow. Pankow's Rathaus-Center walk starts later, at **18:00**.

items.q: Can we join a lantern walk without a Kita or a church connection?
items.a: Yes. The public walks on the map are open to any family, and parishes do not ask which church you belong to. For a **small walk in your own Kiez**, ask at your Kita or school door and look at your nearest church's noticeboard.

items.q: What happens at a Berlin Laternenumzug?
items.a: A short service, story or play about St. Martin sharing his cloak, then a **slow walk of about half an hour to an hour** with songs, often behind a rider on a horse, and at the end a **Martinsfeuer**, warm punch and **Martinshörnchen** to share.

Roast goose with **red cabbage and dumplings**, which many German restaurants serve around 11 November, usually for two or four people and often only with a reservation. For the weekend of 14 and 15 November, **book this week**.
